title: Multi-gene calibrated PPI with shared clusters
problem: Calibrated interval inference for J parallel PPI tasks (genes) whose estimators are NOT independent because all tasks are computed on the same G labelled clusters (donors). Stated gaps in the multi-task PPI/empirical-Bayes line: (i) Empirical Bayes rebiasing models per-task bias as exchangeable draws from an unknown law, treats estimators as exactly normal with known second moments and does not propagate CLT error or plug-in error in the variances; (ii) the authors flag that bias exchangeability can fail; (iii) PAS needs average-coverage intervals centred at the shrinkage estimator; (iv) cross-task recalibration PPI is to be combined with shrinkage 'as future work'. None treats tasks that share clusters, so cross-task dependence has rank at most G-1 and G is 4-16. Precise question: with J=50-343 genes and G labelled donors, what interval (t-type finite-G reference, NPMLE bias prior learned across genes, joint covariance across genes) attains average coverage across genes, and when does bias exchangeability across genes hold for a shared-embedding predictor?
source_citation: Ling, Li, Guan & Ignatiadis, Empirical Bayes Rebiasing, arXiv:2605.08069 (May 2026); Li & Ignatiadis, Prediction-Powered Adaptive Shrinkage Estimation, arXiv:2502.14166 (v3 Nov 2025); Emmenegger, Stahler & Podimata, PPI Across Many Tasks, arXiv:2605.29249 (May 2026)
quote_or_paraphrase_location: 2605.08069 Section 7 Conclusion (two flagged limitations: exchangeability of biases; exactly normal estimators, no propagation of CLT or plug-in error). 2502.14166 Section 7 Conclusion: 'a natural next step is to develop average coverage controlling intervals' around PAS (suggests building on Armstrong-Kolesar-Plagborg-Moller); PAS multi-problem setup states independence across problems. 2605.29249 Section 6 Related Work: combining its recalibration with PAS-type shrinkage 'We view this as future work'. My own grep of all three texts found no treatment of clustered units or tasks sharing units.
why_fits_this_project: This is the one structure the ST project has that the benchmark datasets of these papers (Amazon products, LM Arena, GWAS) lack: hundreds of parallel estimands computed on the same few donors, with a full-label ground truth for every gene, so average-coverage claims can be checked directly. Few labelled clusters is exactly the regime where the normal approximation they ignore fails. It also gives the paper a methodological core (a procedure plus a coverage theorem) rather than a regime comparison.
scoop_risk: Medium. The Ignatiadis lab has three related preprints in 8 months and 'Rebiasing' is still a draft manuscript, so a clustered extension is plausible for them, but none of the three papers mentions clusters, donors or shared units (my keyword scan). Search-based check only, provisional.
data_in_hand_fit: Yes, not yet run. HEST tasks: leave-donor-out FM predictions for 50-343 genes, 14-24 donors; draw n_L=4-16 donors, build per-gene intervals, score average coverage and width against the all-donor truth; estimate the bias distribution across genes and test exchangeability (bias vs truth, vs predictor R^2). ACS: use many subgroup means (e.g. occupation or age bands) as tasks, states as clusters.

title: HCP/GHCP under spatial within-donor dependence and vector outcomes
problem: Prediction sets for a new spot (or new cell) of a new donor when the spots of a donor are spatially dependent, hence not exchangeable, and when the outcome is a vector (many genes). HCP, GHCP and the hierarchical conformal selection methods all assume that observations within a group are exchangeable or i.i.d. given the group law. Stated open directions are more complex within-group structure (time series, vectors of multiple outcomes) and group-feature-conditional guarantees. Precise question: what block-exchangeable or spatial-subsampling version of HCP/GHCP has finite-sample or asymptotic coverage for a new spot in an unseen donor, how much does naive HCP under-cover on real tissue, and how are simultaneous sets over J genes built without paying a J-fold Bonferroni price?
source_citation: Lee & Ren, Selection from Hierarchical Data with Conformal e-values, arXiv:2501.02514; Mallick, Tchetgen Tchetgen, Dobriban & Lee, Generalized Hierarchical Conformal Prediction (GHCP), arXiv:2608.15500; Lee, Barber & Willett, Distribution-free inference with hierarchical data, arXiv:2306.06342; adjacent: Sen & Saha, Conformal Prediction for Spatially Dependent Data via Sequential Whitening, arXiv:2610.10168
quote_or_paraphrase_location: 2501.02514 Section 7 Discussion: asks about 'more complex within-group data structures, such as time series or vectors of multiple outcomes for each group' and group-feature-conditional FDR; 2608.15500 Section 1.1 Assumption A3 (within-group i.i.d.) and Section 4 Discussion (lists only group-size ignorability, donor selection with covariates, data-adaptive mergers, less conservative derandomisation; spatial dependence is NOT listed, so the gap is my inference); 2306.06342 Section 5 Discussion (what additions make useful distribution-free inference possible).
why_fits_this_project: Directly the project's prediction-set-for-new-cluster problem, but with the two features that make ST different from ACS: spatially dependent units inside a cluster and 50-343 outcomes at once. The project already has HCP, GHCP and the target donor's own full conformal set in its prediction-set map, so this extends existing code rather than starting over.
scoop_risk: Low to medium. The Barber/Willett/Lee/Ren group could extend within-group structure, and a spatial conformal paper appeared on 2026-10-07 (not hierarchical, not donor-level). ST is not the application of any of these papers. Search-based, provisional.
data_in_hand_fit: Yes, not yet run. HEST Visium (hex lattice) and Xenium coordinates with leave-donor-out predictions: measure coverage of HCP/GHCP by donor and gene, compare with spatial-block calibration; ACS PUMS by state serves as the exchangeable control case.

title: PPI for within-cluster pairwise (U-statistic) estimands
problem: Prediction-powered inference for estimands that are U-statistics within clusters, such as gene-gene correlation within a donor, spatial autocorrelation (Moran-type) of a gene, intraclass correlation or between-donor variance of a gene, with few labelled clusters. The active-inference U-statistic paper treats i.i.d. units, non-degenerate kernels, asymptotics only, and lists finite-sample guarantees and the degenerate regime as open. A separate 2026 paper gives clustered-data limit theory for U-statistics without predictions. The combination (prediction-powered, cluster-robust, few clusters) is not in either.
source_citation: Wang, Huo, Peng & Zou, Learning U-Statistics with Active Inference, arXiv:2605.11638; Tsyawo, Limit Theory for U-Statistics under Clustered and Weakly Dependent Data, arXiv:2608.18443
quote_or_paraphrase_location: 2605.11638 Section 5 Discussion: finite-sample guarantees for learned sampling policies 'remain an important direction'; identifying optimal sampling rules in the degenerate regime 'remains an open and challenging problem'. The word 'cluster' does not occur in the text. 2608.18443 Section 4.1: cluster-robust projection covariance. The combination is my inference, not a statement by either paper.
why_fits_this_project: Spatial transcriptomics questions are rarely about means: co-expression, spatial autocorrelation and between-donor heterogeneity are pairwise functionals. Per-donor U-statistics aggregate at cluster level, so cluster-level theory (few clusters) is the same technology the project already uses.
scoop_risk: Medium. The combination is an obvious one for either group, and Tsyawo's clustered theory lowers the effort. Search-based, provisional.
data_in_hand_fit: Yes, not yet run. Xenium lung (14 donors): per-donor gene-gene correlations for gene pairs among the 50-343 genes; Visium: per-slide Moran's I with leave-donor-out predictions; ACS: income-education correlation by state.

title: Conformal selection for a new donor with hierarchical exchangeability
problem: Select spots (or gene-spot pairs) in a new donor whose measured expression exceeds a threshold, with FDR control, using foundation-model predictions and labelled donors for calibration, under hierarchical rather than i.i.d. exchangeability. The hierarchical conformal e-value paper handles group-level and individual-level selection but states group-feature-conditional control, multi-outcome vectors and richer within-group structure as open; its subsampling method uses only between-group exchangeability. Conformal-selection follow-ups of 2025-26 (multi-condition, optimised scores, noisy labels) were seen only as abstracts or snippets.
source_citation: Lee & Ren, Selection from Hierarchical Data with Conformal e-values, arXiv:2501.02514 (base method: Jin & Candes, Selection by prediction with conformal p-values, JMLR 2023, not read in full)
quote_or_paraphrase_location: Section 7 Discussion: group feature-conditional FDR in a distribution-free sense; extension to more complex within-group structures such as time series or vectors of multiple outcomes; 'we leave these questions for future work'.
why_fits_this_project: 'Which spots are marker-positive or in a tumour-like programme in this new donor' is a natural ST task and uses the same hierarchical calibration machinery as the prediction sets, so it can be developed in the same paper as the previous prediction-set row.
scoop_risk: Medium. Same authors' natural next step; many groups publish on conformal selection (at least four 2025-26 variants seen), but none seen is hierarchical plus spatial.
data_in_hand_fit: Yes, not yet run. Threshold per gene at a high quantile of measured expression; leave-donor-out calibration across labelled donors; check FDR across donors on HEST; ACS: Lee & Ren already use ACS income groups (Section 6.1), so use a different ACS target.

title: Shrinkage across donors/areas (per-cluster PPI) with few tasks
problem: Per-cluster estimands (a donor's mean or within-donor slope, a state's mean) estimated from the few labelled spots in each cluster plus predictions for all spots, borrowing strength across the m clusters by empirical Bayes. Open: intervals with average-coverage control around PAS-type estimators; behaviour when the number of tasks m is only 14-50 so that nonparametric g-modelling is unstable; within-task dependence among spots. A 2026 design-based spatial PPI paper listed model-assisted small-area estimation (shrinking the rectifier across areas, with the prediction map as auxiliary) as an extension, and later dropped it from its Discussion.
source_citation: Li & Ignatiadis, arXiv:2502.14166; Shirota, Design-Based Prediction-Powered Inference for Spatial Data, arXiv:2608.10356 v1 (v2 retitled 'Conditional validity of prediction-powered inference for spatially dependent finite populations')
quote_or_paraphrase_location: 2502.14166 Section 7 Conclusion (average-coverage intervals around PAS). 2608.10356v1 Section 7 Discussion, 'The third is small-area estimation' paragraph (rectifier shrinkage across areas; gap does not shrink with the number of labels); this paragraph is absent from the later version I fetched.
why_fits_this_project: Treats donors or states as the small areas. Matches the project's within-donor slope estimands and the finding that predictors add little there, where shrinkage across donors may add more than predictions do.
scoop_risk: Medium. Both authors named the direction; PAS is being extended by the same lab (see multi-gene row). Few tasks makes the EB machinery less attractive, which lowers the competition.
data_in_hand_fit: Yes, not yet run. HEST: per-donor means/slopes, 14-24 donors, truth from all labels; ACS: 51 states, PUMAs within.

title: Hierarchical conformal: number of groups vs observations per group
problem: The study-design question for distribution-free prediction sets: for a fixed labelling budget, many calibration groups K with few observations N_k each, or few groups with many. HCP's authors call characterising this tradeoff important and leave it open; it has no formula for how width and coverage slack depend on (K, N_k, between-group share of score variance).
source_citation: Lee, Barber & Willett, Distribution-free inference with hierarchical data, arXiv:2306.06342 (listed as to appear in the ACM/IMS Journal of Data Science on the authors' page)
quote_or_paraphrase_location: Section 5 Discussion: 'Characterizing the pros and cons of this tradeoff is an important question' for the choice between many groups with few repeats and few groups with many.
why_fits_this_project: The same regime question as the PPI paper (whole clusters vs few units per cluster) but for prediction sets. The project's own prediction-set map already covers part of it (HCP vs the target donor's own set, switch at 9 labelled spots), so the open part is a closed-form or sharp characterisation, not another simulation.
scoop_risk: Medium. Stated since 2023 and unclaimed in GHCP (Aug 2026), but easy for the HCP group; partial overlap with the project's existing map.
data_in_hand_fit: Yes: ACS by state (51 groups, large N_k) and HEST (14-24 donors, thousands of spots). Already partly run in the project.

title: Active (PPS) labelling of clusters with valid inference, many estimands
problem: Choose which clusters to label with data-dependent but known inclusion probabilities, using prediction uncertainty at cluster level, with valid inference at G=14-50 and n_L=4-16 (heavy-tailed Horvitz-Thompson weights, effective sample size). Broska & Howes require label probabilities independent of the data and propose active labelling of clusters as future work. Ma & Candes state joint design for several estimands (trace or determinant of the joint covariance) as future work for unit-level policies. In ST one labelled donor yields all genes at once, so the criterion is a scalar summary of a J-dimensional covariance.
source_citation: Broska & Howes, Cluster-Robust Prediction-Powered Inference, arXiv:2610.09601; Ma & Candes, OPAL, arXiv:2606.03211; Zrnic & Candes, Active Statistical Inference, arXiv:2403.03208
quote_or_paraphrase_location: 2610.09601 Section 4 Conclusion, third limitation (labels must not depend on predictions or labels already collected; active labelling of clusters named); 2606.03211 Section 6.1 (multiple estimands, tr(W Sigma) or det Sigma, 'promising direction for future work'). Zrnic & Candes: the HTML I fetched has no Discussion section, so nothing is quoted from it.
why_fits_this_project: High: the project studies cluster selection already (rejective/Mahalanobis, cube, k-center), which is prior art. What is new is a prediction-driven PPS design for clusters with its few-cluster interval and a multi-gene criterion.
scoop_risk: High. Named by the Broska/Howes authors, whose acknowledgements thank Candes and Zrnic, and the multi-estimand version is named by Ma & Candes. Project prior art on balanced selection already covers part of the ground.
data_in_hand_fit: Yes, not yet run: leave-donor-out residual scales per donor and gene as the uncertainty score; compare to uniform and balanced selection on the all-donor truth.

title: Spatial PPI on irregular tissue domains with discontinuous prediction-error fields
problem: Conditional validity of PPI for a spatially dependent finite population when the domain is irregular and the prediction-error field is discontinuous (tissue edges, tumour/stroma boundaries). The author states that no result covers irregular sites or discontinuous map boundaries and that the proven spectral-basis conditions need smooth, periodic designs. Spot-level partial labelling inside one slide is the natural ST version.
source_citation: Shirota, Conditional validity of prediction-powered inference for spatially dependent finite populations, arXiv:2608.10356 (later version; v1 titled Design-Based Prediction-Powered Inference for Spatial Data); Salerno, Wu & McCormick, arXiv:2603.11368
quote_or_paraphrase_location: 2608.10356 Section 7 Discussion and evidential scope: 'no result verifies the conditions for irregular LUCAS sites or discontinuous map boundaries'; 2603.11368 Section 7 Conclusions: conditions for jackknife-HAC to be asymptotically equivalent to HAC and finite-sample robustness with limited labels.
why_fits_this_project: Moderate: the project labels whole clusters, while this problem is about labelled spots inside one slide, so it would be a second track. Strongest for the design-based target in the brief.
scoop_risk: Low to medium. Single-author preprint that changed substantially between versions; ST not its application.
data_in_hand_fit: Partly, not yet run. HEST has spot coordinates and leave-donor-out predictions per slide, enough for within-slide labelled-spot experiments; the project's cluster-level tasks do not use them.

title: Compound-randomisation / moderated-t FDR for donor-level contrasts with PPI and dependent genes
problem: Finite-sample FDR-controlled testing of thousands of genes with a handful of replicates, here donors, when scores are augmented by foundation-model predictions and genes are dependent. Ignatiadis & Roquain's guarantee needs independence across units and null group invariance; their cited Barber & Samworth calibration has the same structure. The TIDEST paper (valid DE on imputed ST, not from histology) lists multiple conditions and hierarchical study designs as open.
source_citation: Ignatiadis & Roquain, Empirical Bayes prepivoting under group invariance, arXiv:2609.26764; TIDEST, PMC13320745 (2026)
quote_or_paraphrase_location: 2609.26764 abstract and Introduction footnote 1: 'Here we assume independence across units'; Section 9 Discussion does not list this as open, so the gap is my inference. TIDEST Discussion paragraph beginning 'Several limitations warrant consideration': hierarchical study designs listed as a direction for future research. A bioRxiv PPI-for-DE paper (CSDE) was seen only as a search snippet (page returned HTTP 429).
why_fits_this_project: Genes are the units and donors the replicates, the exact reverse of the PPI setting, so this tests whether the project's few-cluster skew finding also breaks group-invariance (symmetric-null) calibration.
data_in_hand_fit: Uncertain. Needs a donor-level group variable (e.g. tumour vs normal); I have not checked which HEST tasks carry one. Gene dependence can be studied on all tasks.

title: Common benchmark for clustered PPI with explicit labelling mechanism
problem: Mozer's fourth suggestion: evaluate PPI and model-assisted estimators on common benchmarks where the target, the labelling mechanism and the unlabelled pool are explicit. No such benchmark exists for clustered data with real predictors.
source_citation: Mozer, PPI is the Difference Estimator, arXiv:2603.19160
quote_or_paraphrase_location: Section 5 Discussion, list of four suggestions, item 4.
why_fits_this_project: The HEST tasks plus ACS PUMS with leave-donor-out predictions are such a benchmark; the project could release it.
scoop_risk: Low, but it is a resource contribution, not a statistical result, so it is weak for the stated goal.

title: Single-fit PPI with variance correction (no cross-fitting) at few clusters
problem: Lee & Kim propose SF-PPI-VC, valid without cross-fitting through an explicit variance correction, for i.i.d. or simple-random samples, and leave PPI++ for later. With 4-16 labelled clusters cross-fitting costs half of them, so a clustered SF-PPI-VC would remove that cost.
source_citation: Lee & Kim, Statistical Optimality of Prediction-Powered Inference, arXiv:2606.08730
quote_or_paraphrase_location: Section 2: 'A full treatment is left for future work' (PPI++); Section 5.3 defines SF-PPI-VC. No future-work section; the clustered extension is my inference.
why_fits_this_project: Matches the project's observation that cross-fitting the tuning slope on half the labelled clusters is costly. Their set-up also separates the finite-population root from the super-population root, the two targets of the brief.
scoop_risk: Medium to high; project already has exactly unbiased split-sample forms (Williams) and cross-fitted versions.

title: Cross-fitted model-assisted ML under two-stage cluster designs
problem: Design-based confidence intervals for cross-fitted ML model-assisted estimators under multi-stage cluster sampling with few primary units, including the order of second-phase variance for adaptive learners. An et al. treat single-stage designs; no 'two-stage', 'multistage' or 'cluster sampling' string occurs in An et al., the Dagdoug-Haziza review (2604.01160) or Riano (checked by keyword scan); Riano states that design-based interval coverage for a related program is open and that variance estimation with ML predictors is a central open question for survey statisticians.
source_citation: An, Dagdoug, Haziza & Tille, arXiv:2609.10904; Riano, arXiv:2609.04082; Dagdoug & Haziza, arXiv:2604.01160
quote_or_paraphrase_location: 2609.10904 Section 8 Final remarks (extensions to estimating equations left to future work, 'detailed study of these extensions in future work'); 2609.04082 Introduction and Section 7 Discussion (order of E_p(V_2) for adaptively refitted trees 'open').
why_fits_this_project: The design-based target of the brief with states or PUMAs as primary units.
scoop_risk: Medium to high. The Haziza/Dagdoug/Tille group is active, and the project already knows Karim (2606.30918, PSU-level cross-fitting).
data_in_hand_fit: Yes: ACS by state/PUMA; HEST with donors as primary units.

title: Small-sample (few-cluster) cluster-robust PPI intervals and cluster bootstrap theory
problem: Small-sample correction or wild cluster bootstrap for PPI++ when few clusters are labelled; theoretical justification of the cluster bootstrap for predict-then-debias, left out of scope by its authors.
source_citation: Broska & Howes, arXiv:2610.09601; Kluger, Lu, Zrnic, Wang & Bates, arXiv:2501.18577
quote_or_paraphrase_location: 2610.09601 Section 4 Conclusion, first limitation (no small-sample correction; wild cluster bootstrap named). 2501.18577 Section 3.4 and Appendix B: 'Theoretical justifications of Algorithms 5 and 6 are out of scope for the current work.'
why_fits_this_project: Exactly the project's headline difficulty, but the project's own record already treats the t reference, CR2, wild bootstrap and Johnson's skewness-modified t as classical.
scoop_risk: High: named as next steps by two author groups, and the correction is classical.

title: GHCP extensions: informative group size, covariate-aware donors, adaptive mergers
problem: GHCP's own list: validity when group size depends on the group law, donor selection using group covariates, data-adaptive global-local mergers with finite-sample validity, and less conservative derandomisation.
source_citation: Mallick, Tchetgen Tchetgen, Dobriban & Lee, arXiv:2608.15500
why_fits_this_project: Informative group size is real in both datasets (spots per slide, state population), and the paper already uses ACS PUMS income.
scoop_risk: High: same authors' stated next steps, same dataset, v1 only.

title: Cost model for allocation across and within clusters
problem: Broska & Howes give variance formulas for labelling designs but no cost model, so allocation across and within clusters under a budget is left open.
why_fits_this_project: This is the regime comparison the project already did; it is classical two-stage sampling with costs.
